title: Solid, Liquid, Gas

definition.heading: What is matter?
definition.text: Everything around us is made of matter. Matter is anything that takes up space and has weight. Matter comes in three main states: solid, liquid and gas. The tiny particles inside matter move in different ways in each state.

states.name: Solid
states.summary: A solid has its own shape and its own size.
states.explain: The tiny particles in a solid are packed close together and can only wiggle in place. That is why a solid does not change shape when you put it in a different container.
states.try_it: Put a pencil in a box and then in a bag. Does the pencil change its shape?

states.name: Liquid
states.summary: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.
states.explain: The particles in a liquid are close together but they slide past each other. That is why a liquid can be poured and always has a flat top surface.
properties: Takes the shape of its container
states.try_it: Pour the same water into a glass and then into a bowl. What happens to its shape?

states.name: Gas
states.summary: A gas spreads out and fills all the space it can.
states.explain: The particles in a gas are far apart and zoom around very fast. A gas has no shape and no fixed size. It fills a balloon, a ball or a whole room.
properties: Has no shape of its own
states.try_it: Blow up a balloon. The air inside spreads to fill the whole balloon!

changes: A solid turns into a liquid when it is heated. Ice melts into water.
A liquid turns into a gas when it is heated a lot. Water boils into steam.
A liquid turns into a solid when it gets very cold. Water freezes into ice.
A gas turns into a liquid when it cools. Steam on a cold lid becomes water drops.
